package_info.why_malicious: The package contains multi-layered, obfuscated JavaScript that fetches and executes additional malware from the internet, including scripts that exfiltrate sensitive data and install further payloads. It abuses npm lifecycle scripts to trigger malicious actions during installation or build, and employs anti-forensic techniques to evade detection.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the postinstall script executes install.js, which initiates the malware chain by downloading and executing further payloads from remote servers.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Abuse of the postinstall script to run arbitrary code is a common malware technique, especially when the code is obfuscated or fetches remote content.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely require network access or remote code execution during installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages use postinstall for setup or dependency checks, but not for downloading and executing remote code.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code fetches a remote JavaScript payload from ipcheck.cloud and executes it using eval, enabling dynamic delivery and execution of malicious code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and executing remote code at runtime is a hallmark of malware, especially when using eval.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not execute code from untrusted remote sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic plugin systems may fetch code, but with strict validation and not via eval.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code spawns a PowerShell process to download, decrypt, and execute further payloads, escalating the attack chain and enabling cross-platform infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Spawning PowerShell from Node.js is highly unusual and often used for malicious purposes.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate JavaScript packages do not invoke PowerShell for arbitrary code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare in legitimate use; sometimes for cross-platform scripting in devops tools.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the PowerShell script downloads a binary payload, decrypts it using XOR, and loads it as a DLL via reflection, enabling in-memory execution of malware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading, decrypting, and loading DLLs in-memory is a classic malware technique to evade disk-based detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal scripts do not perform in-memory DLL loading from remote sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare in legitimate automation or red-team tools.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After payload execution, the script deletes the downloaded payload file to remove forensic evidence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Immediate deletion of artifacts is an anti-forensic technique to hinder investigation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts do not erase their own payloads post-execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare, except in some self-cleaning installers.

attack_chain.action: Malicious postinstall script triggers execution of install.js during npm install.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of remote JavaScript payload.

attack_chain.action: install.js fetches and executes obfuscated JavaScript from a remote malicious domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of further malicious logic, including process spawning.

attack_chain.action: Obfuscated JavaScript spawns a PowerShell process to download and execute additional payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: PowerShell script execution and payload delivery.

attack_chain.action: PowerShell script downloads, decrypts, and loads a DLL payload in-memory.
PowerShell script deletes the downloaded payload to erase forensic evidence.

behavioral_signatures: npm postinstall script triggers network requests
JavaScript code using eval on remote content
PowerShell scripts downloading and decrypting payloads
file_indicators: scripts/install.js with obfuscated or network-fetching code
temporary files in %TEMP% or /tmp/ related to payloads
network_indicators: HTTP(S) requests to non-standard domains during install or runtime
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that initiate network connections or execute obfuscated code. Flag any use of eval on remote content, especially from suspicious domains. Detect Node.js processes spawning PowerShell or other shell interpreters. Watch for PowerShell scripts that download, decrypt, and load DLLs in-memory, and for immediate deletion of payload files after execution. Correlate with known IoCs and domains.
